title: WATCHERS OF WHAT IS HAPPENING
purpose: Document public GitHub witnesses and repositories around the 2026-08-26/28 Actions scheduler/control-plane anomaly, compare their fingerprints with the JANUS Record Drift Observatory, audit JANUS as a possible contributor, and preserve a separate Russian-services comparison lane without conflating correlation with causation.
epistemic_firewall: Public handle is not a real-world identity; do not infer name, employer, country, or motive unless explicitly published and relevant.
A similar symptom is not proof of a shared root cause.
A coincident outage on another provider is not proof of a coordinated attack.
Repository names marked PRIVATE_OR_UNDISCLOSED or UNKNOWN must not be guessed.
Second-hand repository references are kept separate from first-hand witness testimony.
JANUS is not exempt from suspicion; its own event generation is audited using the same standards.
Runs and jobs are different accounting units; platform-scale comparisons are order-of-magnitude context only.

github_actions_2026_08_26.core_finding: GitHub reported saturation of writes to the database primary used by the service processing Actions workflow triggers. A primary failover did not fully recover the system. GitHub attributed the saturation to growing daily peak load combined with an upstream issue in its event-processing infrastructure that amplified bursts.
github_actions_2026_08_26.throttling_interpretation: Backpressure/load shedding: reduce admitted inbound event/work rate below the distressed system's sustainable processing rate, restart services, drain backlog, then gradually raise the admission limit. GitHub said the downstream throttles had been set about 10% too high to protect the system, so the guardrail admitted more load than the degraded path could safely absorb.

github_schedule_documentation.finding: GitHub documents that scheduled events can be delayed under high load and, if load is sufficiently high, some queued jobs may be dropped; start-of-hour is a known high-load period.
github_schedule_documentation.relevance: Several witness cases use off-hour minutes (:17, :23, :30), so ordinary top-of-hour delay does not fully explain multi-hour materialization delays or dozens of consecutive missing run objects.

fingerprint: Once the run object exists, runner queue is 0 seconds.
Cron minute :17 is not at the top of the hour.
Stored record drift remained unconfirmed; this is an operational scheduler observation.
